**Finding submitted: MISSING (medium severity)**

**What I found.** The Agreement has no transition-assistance or data-return provision anywhere:

- **Article XXI (Effect of Termination, p0138)** runs one way only — licenses terminate automatically, and *we* must ship all Licensed Technology, APIs, documentation and Confidential Information to Licensor within five days plus officer certification. It closes with "All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination," with no reciprocal obligation on Licensor.
- **Article X confidentiality (p0124)** binds only the Licensee and contains no return/destruction mechanic that could partially serve.
- The other termination provisions — Article XIX insolvency (p0132–33), Article XX change of control (p0134–37), Article XXIII (p0142) — are silent on exit mechanics.

**Why it matters here.** The Licensed Technology is a hosted platform through which we receive consolidated market data and enter trading tickets (p0021, p0033), so our order, trade and account records reside on Licensor's systems. With no export right, termination would leave us unable to recover them — at or near the playbook's walk-away position.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** New subsection (c) inserted after p0138 at the preferred position: up to six (6) months of transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, return of our data within thirty (30) days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter. The comment flags 90 days of assistance as an acceptable fallback provided the 30-day data return survives.
